newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says leading rebels killed after tip-offs.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says leading rebels killed after tip-offs.

text.p: Algerian security forces, helped by tip-offs in return for hefty government rewards, have shot dead four Moslem rebel leaders along with 13 fellow guerrillas, an Algerian official statement said on Saturday.
Among those killed was Tayeb Djerriri, alias Djaafar, killed with five other rebels in the Western province of Sidi Bel Abbes, the Algerian security forces said.
The Algerian authorities had last week offered residents three million dinars ($53,571) for information leading to the capture or the killing of Tayeb.

In Algiers, security forces killed a rebel leader in the Algerian capital named as Yahia Rihane, alias Abdellah Krounfel, for whom the authorities offered two million dinars ($35,714) for information leading to his slaying or capture.

Mohamed Bengharsallah, a leading Moslem guerrilla figure, was shot dead by security forces with seven other rebels in the eastern town of Constantine, added the statement carried by the official Algerian news agency APS.
The authorities had put up one million dinars ($17,857) reward for tip-off leading security forces to the arrest or the slaying of Bengharsallah.

The Algerian security forces said the fourth guerrilla leader Farid Chekchoukh, alias Dadiche, was shot dead near Ouled Yaiche village in the province of Blida, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.Another rebel was killed with him.
The authorities had offered one million dinars reward for Chekchoukh.
The statement said that Rihane was shot dead on Thursday in Algiers but gave no date for the killing of the other rebels.

About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
